title: zcc_list_devices dropped policy_name and other enrollment fields since v0.13.0 (regression)

blocks.heading: zcc_list_devices dropped policy_name and other enrollment fields since v0.13.0 (regression)

blocks.text: Starting with v0.13.0, the zcc_list_devices tool returns only a shaped, 6-field device summary. The policy_name field — along with most other enrollment and telemetry fields — is no longer included in the response. This is a breaking change for any workflow that relied on per-device policy information, and there is currently no lternative tool that exposes it.
Both endpoints were verified live: on 0.12.7 the field is present, on 0.13.3 it is absent.

The regression was introduced in commit 4a2d83a (https://github.com/zscaler/zscaler-mcp-server/commit/4a2d83a8a3875b67d04ef1943d307e4d5bbfb5b3) (PR #82, "agent-first shaping, Zscaler Cellular (ZCell) service, and guided prompts"), first shipped in v0.13.0 (2026-07-10).
The device record used to be returned as-is; it is now projected through a DeviceSummary model:
# v0.12.7 — full SDK record, plus JMESPath support results = [d.as_dict() for d in devices] return apply_jmespath(results, query)
# v0.13.0+ — projected down to a fixed summary return shape_many([d.as_dict() for d in (devices or [])], _shape_device)
Retained (v0.13.x): udid, user, machine_hostname, os_version, agent_version, registration_state

Removed: policy_name, deregistration_timestamp, registration_time, keep_alive_time, last_seen_time, owner, mac_address, vpn_state, tunnel_version, and the remaining fields of the ~40-field enrollment record.
The query (JMESPath) parameter was also removed in the same change, so client-side projection/filtering is no longer available as a workaround.

blocks.item: Per-device / per-user policy assignment can no longer be determined through the MCP server on v0.13.x.
No other tool fills the gap: zcc_list_forwarding_profiles lists tenant-wide forwarding profiles (id, name, active status) but does not map a profile to a device
The removal of query means callers cannot even project the fields themselves from a richer payload.
Run the server on any v0.13.x release.
Observe that every device object contains only the 6 summary fields, with no policy_name.
Restore the removed fields — re-include policy_name and the other enrollment/telemetry fields in the default response, or
Provide an opt-in — e.g. a verbose/full flag on zcc_list_devices that returns the complete SDK record, and/or restore the query parameter so callers can select
Add a dedicated tool for per-device policy assignment.
zscaler-mcp-server — reproduced on 0.13.3; confirmed working on 0.12.7.

blocks.text: :tada: This issue has been resolved in version 0.14.0 :tada:
The release is available on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/zscaler-mcp/) and [GitHub release](https://github.com/zscaler/zscaler-mcp-server/releases/tag/v0.14.0)
